findings.claim: field() turns any truthy non-list value at a [] path into a list of one, so `sources: src/a.py` (a bare string) or a single sources mapping now yields a resource. The old _sources returned [] for any non-list sources, so review_due now checks git history for concepts it used to skip. The plan says field keeps today's forms; the single-mapping case was only meant for verified.

test_manifesto_marks_i4_enforced checks the log with r'I4.*enforced|`manifesto`' on the last dated section, and the I1/I3 line in that section already contains `manifesto`, so the test passes with the I4 log line deleted. r5's fails_when names a missing log line.

ALLOWED_FIELDS cites the wrong spec sections for two keys: the pinned validator puts `verified` under section 5.2 (5.3 is trust tiers) and root-index `okf_version` under section 12, not 8 (section 8 says a non-root index carries no front matter).

The reads scan only recognises a bare-name front_matter(...) call, so `okf.front_matter(p).get('title')` or an alias such as `fm = front_matter` reads front matter without the test noticing. Nothing in src does this today.
